title: InvestED, in order: a Rule #1 course
source: InvestED: The Rule #1 Podcast (Phil Town and Danielle Town), https://feeds.megaphone.fm/investedpodcast

modules.title: Orientation
modules.goal: Why Rule #1 investing, who's teaching, and how the course works.
modules.lesson: Rule #1 is Buffett's *don't lose money*. Everything in this course protects the downside first, then looks for a wonderful business at about half of what it's worth (a $10 bill for $5). Expect investing to teach you about yourself as much as about markets.

modules.title: Understand the business
modules.goal: Circle of competence, the three circles, reading 10-Ks, and investing in line with your values.
modules.lesson:
Munger's four filters run in order, and **understanding** comes first: if you can't understand the business, stop.

1. **Find ideas without throwing darts.** Events (scary industry news) and great investors' buys point you somewhere. Treat them as tips, never as decisions.
2. **Start inside your circles.** Overlap what you love, what you're good at and where you make and spend money.
3. **Learn what a manager would know.** Read industry books for the key numbers, then several years of 10-K *Business* and *MD&A*, then the top competitors' filings.
4. **Check your values.** You're buying a piece of the whole company and you vote with that money, so prefer simple, hard-to-ruin businesses you'd like to see thrive for 20 years.
5. **Respect the edge.** Losses happen at the boundary of your competence. When you feel the tension or the 10-K stays murky, put the idea in the *too-hard* pile.

modules.title: Moats
modules.goal: The five moats (brand, secret, toll bridge, switching, price), how to spot a durable competitive advantage, and how to tell when it's eroding.

modules.title: Management
modules.goal: Owner-oriented, honest and capable leaders, and how to judge them from letters, calls and capital allocation.

modules.title: The numbers: Big Five and ROIC
modules.goal: ROIC, sales, EPS, equity (BVPS) and operating cash flow growth, plus debt, and what they reveal about a moat.

modules.title: Valuation and margin of safety
modules.goal: Sticker Price, the MOS price, Payback Time, Ten Cap and the reasoning behind each.

modules.title: Events and buying
modules.goal: Waiting for a business to go on sale, events, buying in tranches and building a watchlist.

modules.title: Psychology and practice
modules.goal: Fear, greed, patience, the tension signal, inversion and avoiding noise.

modules.title: Portfolio and selling
modules.goal: Concentration, position sizing, when the story changes, and when to sell.

modules.title: The masters
modules.goal: Buffett, Munger, Graham, Pabrai, Spier and others: their ideas and their records.

modules.title: Case studies and interviews
modules.goal: Companies analysed on the show, and guests' stories and lessons.

glossary.definition: Don't lose money. Rule #2: don't forget Rule #1 (Buffett).
Meaning (understand it), Moat, Management, Margin of safety: Munger's four filters, applied in order.
The set of businesses you truly understand. Knowing where it ends matters more than how big it is.
Temporary bad news that puts a good business on sale.
Buying far enough below value (Rule #1: 50% of Sticker) that mistakes don't lose you money.
Making the best case against your idea, then rebutting it or walking away.
Buffett's thought experiment: only 20 purchases in a lifetime, so each must count.
Ideas you pass on because you can't understand them well enough.
